title: --json with an unparsable value is JSON mode
lead: `adj show 1 --json=maybe` is a usage error, and today it prints no error object, because `wantsJSON` treats an unparsable `--json=VALUE` as off. Treat every `--json=VALUE` as on unless `strconv.ParseBool` reads it as false. The usage failure then prints the object with code `usage`.
Not in this slice: any other JSON-mode rule from C216 (value positions, `--`, the last one given wins, commands without a json flag); the error codes (C215); `--format` handling for `context`.
findings_note: S42 relay report; owner 2026-10-22 accepted the recommendation to overrule C216 for this case

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
C216 (S42) made an unparsable bool off. The caller wrote `--json`, so they want machine output, and the run fails as a usage error anyway. Printing nothing on stdout leaves a script with no `error.code`. S39 freezes the JSON contract at 1.0, so this has to change before then. The owner overruled C216 on this point on 2026-10-22.

ork does not branch on adj's error codes (checked 2026-10-22: `ork/internal/cache/cache.go:252-260` retries only on `corrupt` and `locked`, which adj never prints, and `ork/internal/adjcli/adjcli.go` keeps the code without branching on it), so the change only affects scripts that read stdout.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/cli/jsonmode.go:61-67` (`wantsJSON`): with a value, `jsonFlag` is true unless `strconv.ParseBool(value)` returns false with no error. Update the doc comment (:31-39).
- `internal/cli/jsonerror_test.go`: add table rows to the detection test (:40-72): `--json=maybe` is on, `--json=` (empty) is on, and `--json=0` and `--json=F` are off, both after a command and before one (nil flag set). Add an end-to-end case: `show 1 --json=maybe` exits 2 with the object, code `usage`, command `show`, and the same stderr as without the flag value.
- `docs/json.md:60-63`: say that a `--json=VALUE` Go cannot read as a bool turns JSON mode on.
- `AGENTS.md`, wherever it describes JSON-mode detection (if it does); `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased, a line in the S42 entry if that is still unreleased, else a new line.
- Catalog C216: edit its body with `slicer catalog edit C216` so that "--json=false (or an unparsable bool) is off" becomes "a value that strconv.ParseBool reads as false is off; an unparsable value is on (owner, 2026-10-22)".

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Table-driven, red first. Use `t.TempDir()` under `.cache/tmp` and an explicit `cli.Env.Root`, with no `os.Chdir`.
- In the `wantsJSON` table, `--json=maybe` and `--json=` are on and `--json=0` and `--json=F` are off, with a flag set and with nil.
- `show 1 --json=maybe` gives one object on stdout, code `usage`, command `show`, exit 2.
- The existing rows for `--json=false` and the last one given wins still pass.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Red tests.
2. Change the one condition in `wantsJSON`.
3. Update the docs and C216.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `. <worktree>/scripts/env.sh; go -C <worktree> test ./...; go -C <worktree> vet ./...; GOOS=windows go -C <worktree> vet ./...; gofmt -l <worktree>/cmd <worktree>/internal` prints nothing.
- Mutation-check: putting back `err == nil && b` makes the new rows fail.
- `adj lint --root <worktree>` is clean, and so is `slicer --root <worktree> check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/<id>` on its own branch. Commit on that branch after `VERDICT: PASS`. No push, no merge, no AI attribution.
